newsitem.title: USA: Integrated Medical backs '97 loss view.
newsitem.headline: Integrated Medical backs '97 loss view.

text.p: Integrated Medical Resources Inc said Wednesday it considers realistic the consensus of analysts estimates of a loss of $0.73 a share in 1997, but added the loss may not be that large.

Asked about the consensus for a loss of $0.73 a share in 1997, compared with a loss of $1.82 in 1996, Chief Financial Officer Beverly Elving said, "The estimate is...realistic, but perhaps on the conservative side. The loss might not be that large."
Elving also said the consensus for a loss of $0.21 a share in the second quarter was "realistic."
Integrated Medical Resources Inc, which operates clinics to diagnose and treat impotence, said it hopes to report a profit before the second quarter of 1998.

"The analysts, I think, have us profitable in (second quarter) 1998. All of our centers become profitable within the first year, but more than half of our 33 centers aren't a year old yet," Troy Burns, chief executive officer, told Reuters. "But they're ramping up very nicely. So we're probably a little more optimistic than the analysts."
Integrated Medical, which spoke at the Piper Jaffray investors conference here Wednesday, expects to open 12 new centers in 1997, for a total at year-end of 41.
Elving added that Integrated Medical's marketing costs in 1997 will be about $6.0 million, up from $4.3 million in 1996.
